trade.structure: Short CA-US 2Y sovereign spread, paper-marked from market_state.rate_rv.CA-US_2Y (CA yield minus US yield). Implementation: short CA_2Y versus long US_2Y, duration-neutral in spread space. Do not migrate the open onto SOFR/CORRA; family stays bond. STIR equivalent (pay 2027 CORRA strip / receive 2027 SOFR strip) is the policy-path cross-check only, not the locked expression, because mixed-curve linear_combo is not a single locked family.
trade.thesis: Canada is too cheap versus the United States on a peer 2Y spread that sits in the left tail of both the 1y and 5y distributions. That is a valuation statement with a policy-path closing mechanism, not a fade of a decline. Verified facts: CA-US_2Y -140bp on 2026-09-17; CORRA 2.29 versus SOFR 3.85; Fed hike delivered to 3.75-4.00%; CRA prices 84-130bp of hikes through 2027; Canada CPI 3% / core near 2%; BoC minutes flag energy pass-through. Inference: overnight 2.29 cannot remain the 2Y anchor once that hiking path or energy pass-through shows up in data, so the spread should rise (become less negative) via higher CA rates relative to US rates. The Jan-2025 analog at -145bp then +25bp over 3m is the working forward template. Unknowns that cap size: CA labor gauge 38 versus US 75 may justify a structurally wider gap; positioning is missing; gauges are repo-retained.
why_now: Official NY Fed SOFR jumped to 3.85% effective 2026-09-17 after the delivered 25bp hike, widening the overnight CA-US gap, yet CA-US_2Y cheapened 15bp in five days (z -2.17) instead of starting to converge.

BoC minutes flag higher energy pass-through and Canada August CPI still holds at 3% with core near 2%; those known facts now transmit through a post-hike US overnight reset rather than through pre-FOMC hike odds.
CRA already prices 48.5bp by Dec-2026 and 122bp by Sep-2027, so the packet's own policy path is the convergence engine; waiting for a new BoC meeting is not required to define the closing mechanism.
Funded seats pay official SOFR 3.85% ACT/360 on the full $100m even if flat; a markable, historically tailed, policy-path-backed RV with analog invalidation clears sitting in cash.

events.rationale: Verified: CA-US 2Y is -140bp as of 2026-09-17, 1y percentile 3.77 and 5y percentile 4.31, while CORRA 2.29 versus SOFR 3.85 and CRA 2027 contracts already imply 84-130bp of Canadian hikes. Inference: that left-tail spread is a peer-normalized dislocation, not a cheap-because-it-fell screen, and should converge by Canada rates rising versus the US because BoC energy pass-through plus still-3% headline CPI make overnight 2.29 an unsustainable 2Y anchor after a known Fed hike. Unknown: CFTC/CME positioning, whether CA labor 38 versus US 75 is a new wider-spread regime, and any REER/PPP fair value (absent from the packet).

holes_in_opposing_case: The CAD-down bloc is not one mechanism. Dollar-king, rate-hawk and trend-follower want CAD lower because the US stays tighter; perma-bear and rate-dove want CAD lower because Canada cannot deliver the already-priced CRA hiking cycle. Those two stories cannot both be the reason USDCAD should rise, and only the second one actually falsifies short CA-US_2Y.

Dollar-king's long USDCAD treats a 74th-percentile pair as the home of a 4th-percentile CA-US 2Y gap. The packet USDCAD~CA-US_2Y residual is weak (r-squared 0.022). Incomplete FX catch-up is not a fair-value gap; it is a noisy residual. Their own invalidation says Canada hiking along the already-priced CRA path does not kill long USDCAD, which concedes they are betting the rate gap stays wide. That is the opposite of a valuation close.

Carry-is-king runs the same short CA-US_2Y I do, then tags CAD lower. If the holding-period engine is Canada catching up along CRA while you receive US 4.76 versus pay CA 3.27, relative policy is CAD-supportive, not CAD-destructive. Their CAD_DOWN is an unneeded USD overlay on a rates RV that does not own USDCAD.

Perma-bear and rate-dove overweight overnight CORRA 2.29 and labor 38 versus the object that is actually priced: CRAU27 3.51 and CRAM27 3.365. Headline CPI is still 3%, BoC minutes flag energy pass-through, and CA activity is 66. Calling a 122bp path a policy error does not make the 5y-tail CA-US 2Y discount fair value; if they are right and CRA is pulled, that is my stated invalidation, not a reason to prefer long USDCAD.

Rate-hawk and trend-follower pay SOFR_2027-09 and then stamp CAD lower as if USD spot were the expression. Their disagreed object is the 4.755 peak and 2028 fade, not CAD. US 2Y is already 99.8th percentile of 1y at 4.76; paying more US duration does not prove the CA-US spread should stay at -140bp, and it fights the US-rates-down leg that helps a short CA-US_2Y close.
Perma-bull is routed on this CAD tag but is not an opposing CAD case: they also have cad_view higher. Their NZDUSD pitch does not discipline CA-US 2Y or USDCAD.

attack: Strongest opposing claim: rate-dove/perma-bear that labor 38 and core near 2% mean Canada cannot deliver the 100bp-plus CRA hiking cycle, so CA rates fall, the CA-US discount is a new regime, and CAD stays offered. That is a real risk I already capped at 61, not a CAD-spot proof.

It still fails as a CAD-down mandate. If CRA is too hawkish, the clean expression is receive CORRA, which those seats already own. Translating that into CAD lower assumes FX, not STIR, is where the policy error pays. The packet does not show USDCAD stretched, and the FX-rates link is weak.

Dollar-king's claim that USDCAD has not 'made' the policy/labor gap is the discovery flag I rejected in Round 1. Spot is the inferior expression of the same discrepancy. Betting CAD lower because the spread is historically cheap is fading the valuation object instead of owning it.

Carry-is-king's Saudi-workaround point cuts the oil tail; it does not erase BoC pass-through language or 3% headline CPI. Reduced extreme-oil odds are not a reason to attach CAD_DOWN to a short CA-US_2Y that profits if Canada rates rise relative to the US.

Rate-hawk/trend CAD_DOWN is a USD-policy stamp, not a CAD valuation. A still-hot US (gauges 72/75/69/74) can keep SOFR bid without forcing CA-US 2Y to remain a 5y left tail if CRA's already-priced catch-up is the relative move.
defense: CAD higher on my card is a rates-parity implication of the closing mechanism, not a USDCAD short. The locked trade remains short CA-US_2Y. I already constructed long USDCAD and discarded it because the mispricing lives in the 1y/5y left-tail spread, not in a 74th-percentile pair.

Verified still: CA-US_2Y -140bp as of 2026-09-17; CORRA 2.29 versus SOFR 3.85; CRA prices 84-130bp of 2027 hikes; Fed hike delivered; Canada CPI 3% / core near 2%; BoC energy pass-through flagged. The market's own CORRA path is the convergence engine. Jan-2025 analog at -145bp then +25bp over 3m remains the working template; Dec-2024 -20bp extension remains the failure analog.

Uncertainty preserved: CA labor 38 versus US 75 can justify a structurally wider discount; CFTC/CME positioning is missing; gauges are dashboard_v8; Saudi workaround reduced the extreme oil tail. Those cap size. They do not flip the expression into long USDCAD.

I concede the CAD-higher implication, and the rates RV, if CRA 2027 implieds collapse toward overnight 2.29 or if Canadian headline/core disinflate without the flagged energy pass-through, leaving the 5y-tail spread as the new peer regime. I do not concede because USDCAD failed to trend to a new high after a known Fed hike.
